body.statement:
Put
\[
 a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}=
 \sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}\left[1\wedge
 \frac B{\lambda_{nm}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right].
\]
There is a universal constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every \(n,m\ge2\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)}
 E_P\!\left[\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)\right]
 \le C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\]
Thus the loose IPW--SVD upper bound holds in the same expected normalized maximum-row loss used by the minimax lower benchmark.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\) in the predictable class and expose cells in the row-major order of \(\mathrm{def:global\mbox{-}filtration}\).  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:ipw\mbox{-}identification}\), each \(E_{ij}\) has conditional mean zero given \(\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\).  Sequential randomization and bounded outcomes give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[(Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij})^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[
 \frac{Y_{ij}(1)^2}{p_{ij}}+
 \frac{Y_{ij}(0)^2}{1-p_{ij}}
 \mathrel{\Big|}\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}\right]\\
 &\le \frac{2B^2}{q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The equality follows by conditioning once more on both potential outcomes and applying \(\mathrm{ass:sequential\mbox{-}randomization}\); both divisions are valid by \(\mathrm{ass:overlap}\).  Since \(M_{ij}=E_P[Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}\mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\), conditional variance is no larger than this conditional second moment.  Moreover, bounded outcomes and overlap give \(|Z^{\mathrm{ipw}}_{ij}|\le B/q\), while conditional Jensen's inequality gives \(|M_{ij}|\le2B\).  Because \(q<1/2\),
\[
 |E_{ij}|\le \frac{2B}{q}.
\]

Introduce the self-adjoint dilation
\[
 \Delta_{ij}=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 0&E_{ij}e_ie_j^\top\\
 E_{ij}e_je_i^\top&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its norm is \(|E_{ij}|\), and its square has diagonal blocks
\(E_{ij}^2e_ie_i^\top\) and \(E_{ij}^2e_je_j^\top\).  Therefore the predictable quadratic variation obeys
\[
 \left\lVert\sum_{i,j}E_P[\Delta_{ij}^2
 \mid\mathbb G_{o(i,j)-1}]\right\rVert
 \le v_{nm}:=\frac{2B^2(n\vee m)}q.
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:tropp\mbox{-}matrix\mbox{-}freedman}\), applied to both signs of this \((n+m)\)-dimensional martingale, gives
\[
 P\{\lVert E\rVert\ge t\}
 \le2(n+m)\exp\!\left\{-\frac{t^2/2}{v_{nm}+R_{nm}t/3}\right\},
 \qquad R_{nm}=\frac{2B}{q}.
\]
The terminal dilation has operator norm \(\lVert E\rVert\).  With \(L_{nm}=\log(2(n+m))\), solving the quadratic inequality gives, for every \(x\ge0\),
\[
 P\!\left\{\lVert E\rVert>
 \sqrt{2v_{nm}(L_{nm}+x)}+
 \frac{2R_{nm}}3(L_{nm}+x)\right\}\le e^{-x}.
\]
Integrating this tail is legitimate because every increment is bounded.  Using
\(\sqrt{L_{nm}+x}\le\sqrt{L_{nm}}+\sqrt x\),
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\,dx=1\), and
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-x}\sqrt x\,dx<\infty\), we obtain
\[
 E_P\lVert E\rVert
 \le C B\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}+
 \frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}
 =:C\eta_{nm}.
 \tag{20}
\]
Every bound is uniform in \(P\).

It remains to pass from operator error to the declared loss without imposing predictability on the singular factors.  Let \(P_U=UU^\top\), and let \((\widehat U,\widehat\Sigma,\widehat V)\) be the leading rank-\(r\) singular triple of \(M+E\).  Exact rank gives \((I-P_U)M=0\).  The signal floor and the singular-value min--max formula imply, on \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\),
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat\Sigma)
 \ge\sigma_r(M)-\lVert E\rVert
 \ge\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert>0.
\]
Projecting \((M+E)\widehat V=\widehat U\widehat\Sigma\) onto the orthogonal complement of \(U\) gives
\[
 \lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert
 \le\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}-\lVert E\rVert}
 \le\frac{2\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}.
\]
Diagonalizing the principal-angle cosines of \(U^\top\widehat U\) and using
\(2(1-\cos x)\le2\sin^2x\) supplies \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) such that
\[
 \lVert\widehat UR-U\rVert
 \le\sqrt2\lVert(I-P_U)\widehat U\rVert.
\]
Off the event \(\{\lVert E\rVert\le\lambda_{nm}/2\}\), the left side is at most two.  Since \(\lVert Q\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\lVert Q\rVert\), the two cases yield the deterministic inequality
\[
 \mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 \le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right).
 \tag{21}
\]
The fixed tie rule ensures that the leading left singular vectors of \(\mathcal P_r(M+E)\) are the chosen leading left singular vectors of \(M+E\).

The map \(x\mapsto1\wedge x\) is concave and nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\).  Jensen's inequality, (20), and \(1\wedge(Cx)\le C(1\wedge x)\) for \(C\ge1\) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 E_P\left[1\wedge\frac{\lVert E\rVert}{\lambda_{nm}}\right]\\
 &\le C\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left[1\wedge\frac B{\lambda_{nm}}
 \left\{\sqrt{\frac{(n\vee m)\log(e(n+m))}{q}}
 +\frac{\log(e(n+m))}{q}\right\}\right]\\
 &=C a^{\mathrm{loose}}_{nm}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the declared class proves the proposition.
body.justification: The first-moment form places recorded IPW--SVD in the same expected-loss criterion as the minimax converse and the hybrid.
body.gap: The operator-norm route is too loose to close the estimator-independent minimax gap.
body.consumer: The proposition is the quantitative input to the IPW branch of the hybrid.
